# Task
## Captain's intent
I want to work on the paper2db repository as well. I want to make sure that there is a robust pipeline that produces classified MC problems from the original paper PDF. So I want the classified empty problems to be in the form of a crop screenshot from the paper. I want to make sure that the cropping is done correctly and the classification is done correctly. Right now there is already some scripts that does that but it's scattered around and it's difficult to use. And I believe there is already a pipeline branch so you can work on the pipeline branch to clean up the entire pipeline and make a PR for it. So present me with evidence that the pipeline really produces correct classification for MC problems and long questions. So if so I can accept if it doesn't work for some problems, but only less than 5%. So only 5% of the questions need human manual tuning. And you should show me the pipeline results step by step. Maybe there involves some different things, putting anchors or things like that. Present me with the pipeline intermediate result as well as the final results in an HTML editor.

## Firstmate spec

Work on the existing `pipeline` branch (already checked out in the primary clone at 99d3b71 with `./pipeline`); continue from that branch tip, do not restart from main. Push `pipeline` (or a clean PR branch based on it) to origin - the branch is not yet on origin/GitHub - then open a PR into `main`.

Goals:
1. One robust, usable end-to-end pipeline from paper PDFs → classified empty problem crops (PNG screenshots cut from the paper), for both MC and long questions (LQ). Prefer the existing `./pipeline` entry; finish cleanup so day-to-day use is that one command, with scripts as internals.
2. Crops must be correct empty question screenshots (no answer bleed, no truncated stems, anchors not on options/diagrams). Classification into syllabus sections must be correct.
3. Quality bar the captain accepts: ≤5% of questions needing human manual tuning. Measure and report this with evidence for MC and LQ separately (and combined if useful). Use existing outputs under `output/`, `classified/`, and intermediate anchor PDFs where present; re-run stages only as needed (`./pipeline --list-stages`, `--years`, `--from`, `--force` as appropriate). Document what counts as a failure (wrong crop, wrong section, uncertain flag, missing crop).
4. Produce a Lavish HTML review that walks the pipeline step by step: intermediate artifacts (e.g. MC anchor PDFs / blue-dot review, page splits, crops) and final classified crops / section banks. Extend or replace `.lavish/` reviews (`scripts/build_lq_lavish_review.py` and any MC counterpart) so the captain can inspect intermediates and finals in one HTML surface. Prefer lavish-axi for the interactive review delivery.
5. Keep human gates for the remaining hard cases (anchors, uncertain.csv) but make them small enough that ≤5% need manual tuning when the pipeline is run as designed.
6. After cleanup + evidence artifacts land, run /no-mistakes through green CI and open the PR. Report the full PR URL and point firstmate at the Lavish HTML path(s) for captain review. Do not merge.

Do not invent a second parallel pipeline; clean and prove the existing one.

  It auto-resolves every gate including ask-user findings with no escalation, and answering your own ask-user finding is a hard rule violation.
